as_of.main_public_rating: Variant B: current stance from own event scores, 90-day window, 30-day half-life, camp cuts at ±20 (score on −100..+100). The «vs. Markt» column is a direction only (more hawkish than priced / less hawkish than priced / in line with pricing / n/a). Figures taken from market pricing, proxy series names and the internal market-relative score are not published.
as_of.vs_markt_rule: Direction is taken from the sign of the unpublished market-relative current score, using the same ±20 cut as the camps. 'in line with pricing' means that score is between −20 and +20. 'n/a' means the 90-day stance could not be mapped to a market path or the member is not classified. The mapping itself is not validated and was judged not to hold; the column is diagnostic.
as_of.official_quote_basis_points: Official-transcript quotes may contain phrases such as '25 basis points' when that is the speaker's own wording. Those hits are not treated as leaks. Figures taken from market pricing, and proxy series names, are forbidden.
as_of.lean_history: Monthly 90-day / 30-day-half-life current stance on own scores (Variant B), as-of each month-end from 2025-05-31 through 2026-10-31, plus the as-of date 2026-11-20. Each point records score, camp, n events in that 90-day window, and a provisional flag (n < 4 or no event). The 2026-11-20 point reproduces the published current score. No market-relative values are stored.

camp_thresholds.own_score_main: Hawk > +20, Centrist −20..+20, Dove < −20 (score points; Variant B; not validated)

as_of.score_formula: 100 * sum(w_i * d_i for observed i) / sum(w_i for all five dimensions) / 2, with d_i in {-2,-1,0,+1,+2}. Unobserved dimensions are not coded 0; their weights remain in the denominator (shrinkage toward 0).
as_of.path_zero: preferred_rate_path 0 is an observed hold / maintain / patient / no-change preference, not a missing value.
as_of.trend: current own-score stance minus structural own-score lean; material at ±15 points.
as_of.reaction_function: Symmetric rubric: + inflation-first / will not look through; − look-through of transitory inflation or employment-binding reaction.

Maintaining this modestly restrictive stance of monetary policy is entirely appropriate to achieve our maximum employment and price stability goals.

official_quotes.title: Hat Tip to the Data
official_quotes.core_quote: This policy stance is appropriate given that inflation has remained above our 2 percent target while the labor market has been generally consistent with maximum employment. official_quotes.title: Navigating Unpredictable Terrain
official_quotes.core_quote: For these reasons, I fully supported the FOMC’s decisions to reduce the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points at each of its past two meetings. I view monetary policy as being modestly restrictive, although somewhat less so than before our recent actions. Therefore, I still see room for a further adjustment in the near term to the target range for the federal funds rate to move the stance of policy closer to the range of neutral, thereby maintaining the balance between the achievement of our two goals.

official_quotes.title: Unwavering Dedication
official_quotes.core_quote: If the economy evolves in a manner broadly consistent with my forecast, one further upward adjustment of the federal funds target range may be appropriate late this year to support a timelier return of inflation to target. But that is just my forecast, and time—and the totality of the data—will tell.

official_quotes.title: Economic Conditions and Monetary Policy
official_quotes.core_quote: The underlying strength of the U.S. economy, the resilient labor market, above target inflation, and some inflation expectations moving higher indicate to me that the FOMC’s modestly restrictive monetary policy remains appropriate. In short, I believe that monetary policy is currently well positioned.

official_quotes.title: U.S. Economic Outlook and Monetary Policy - Jan. 30, 2026
official_quotes.core_quote: I supported the FOMC’s decision earlier this week to maintain the policy rate—the federal funds rate—in the range of 3.5% to 3.75%. I believe that this setting is neutral and is appropriate given my assessment of the baseline path for the economy and balance of risks. With inflation above target and the risks to the outlook evenly balanced, I believe it would be unadvisable to lower the rate into accommodative territory at this time.

official_quotes.title: The Economic Outlook and Monetary Policy – April 1, 2026
official_quotes.core_quote: I supported the FOMC’s recent decision to hold the policy rate in the range of 3.5% to 3.75%. Policy is well positioned to address risks to both dual mandate objectives, and I expect the current setting of the policy rate will remain appropriate for some time.

official_quotes.title: Q&A at Mississippi Bankers Association 2026 Annual Convention
official_quotes.core_quote: In terms of monetary policy, which I guess is what you want to hear, my own views are that there are very plausible scenarios under which the economy would require us to keep the policy rate at its current level for some time. The current policy setting when you adjust the federal funds rate for inflation—the real federal funds rate—is around one-half of 1% or lower, and that is below what the committee believes is the long-term real neutral rate, which is 1%, so we are either neutral in real terms or slightly accommodative in real terms.

official_quotes.title: How Should the Promise of Higher Productivity Growth Change the Reality of Monetary Policy Today?
official_quotes.core_quote: With the real policy rate sitting below the FOMC’s notion of long-run neutral, inflation running meaningfully above target, longer-term inflation expectations drifting higher and the labor market remaining stable, I believe it would be risky to rely on the prospect of higher productivity growth in the future to solve our inflation problem today. However, at present, I believe we should keep our guard up against persistent above-target inflation today, rather than base monetary policy on the hope that we will have higher productivity growth tomorrow.

official_quotes.title: How and Why
official_quotes.core_quote: In my view, a central bank should communicate how it turns incoming information into policy. Note that I’m not talking about forward guidance of a specific policy path, but rather the framework for how and why policy is determined.

official_quotes.title: Remarks on the U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
official_quotes.core_quote: I judge that additional firming of monetary policy will be necessary, and soon.

official_quotes.core_quote: My purpose this evening is to explain why I believe that the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) should reduce our policy rate by 25 basis points at our next meeting. If the slowing of economic and employment growth were to accelerate and warrant moving toward a more neutral setting more quickly, then waiting until September or even later in the year would risk us falling behind the curve of appropriate policy.

My eagerness to move now is supported by my view that monetary policy is moderately restrictive. While I judge that the FOMC should have begun this process in July, based on the data in hand, I don't believe that a cut of larger than 25 basis points is needed in September.

official_quotes.title: Speech by Governor Waller on the economic outlook
official_quotes.core_quote: While I feel confident, based on what I know today, that monetary policy should take another step toward a more neutral setting at the FOMC's next meeting, the path of appropriate policy beyond that point will be influenced by how the conflict between data on economic activity and the labor market is resolved and the expected path of inflation.

official_quotes.title: Speech by Governor Waller on the economic outlook

official_quotes.title: FOMC dissent: preferred lower 25bp

official_quotes.title: Speech by Governor Waller on the economic outlook

Based on this recent data, I would support removing the "easing bias" language in our policy statement to make it clear that a rate cut is no more likely in the future than a rate increase. With regard to future rate cuts, I am going to need to see improvement on inflation or a significant deterioration in the labor market before I would consider reducing the policy rate.

official_quotes.title: Speech by Governor Waller on the economic outlook

official_quotes.title: The Signaling Value of the Summary of Economic Projections

I am pleased to report that members of the FOMC are unambiguous and unanimous: This Committee will deliver price stability.

official_quotes.title: Semiannual Monetary Policy Report to the Congress
official_quotes.core_quote: The members of our Committee have no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation. And we share a resolute commitment to restoring price stability. official_quotes.title: FOMC post-meeting press conference (opening statement and Q&A)
official_quotes.core_quote: Today, as you know, our Committee decided to vote by a 9-to-3 vote to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3½ to 3¾ percent. ... Inflation remains elevated relative to the Committee’s 2 percent goal. ... There is no soft inflation target; there is no soft implicit target—not on this Committee’s watch. There’s only a target, and it’s 2 percent. ... If inflation continues to be elevated through the forecast period, interest rates could well be part of that solution.

official_quotes.title: Keynote remarks at the 2026 Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium
official_quotes.core_quote: A good majority of my colleagues and I thought the wiser course was to await new information in the intermeeting period ... before deciding whether a change in interest rate policy was advisable. ... But, on balance, I would be hard pressed to describe broad financial conditions as restrictive. ... Inflation is running above our 2 percent target. So the Fed's predominant focus right now should be on prices.

official_quotes.title: FOMC post-meeting press conference (opening statement and Q&A)
official_quotes.core_quote: In the meeting just concluded, the FOMC decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by a ¼ percentage point to 3¾ to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve’s dual mandate. ... But inflation remains elevated. Today’s policy action will support a timelier return to the Committee’s 2 percent goal. ... I would be hard pressed to describe broad financial conditions as restrictive. This view was widely shared by the Committee. So we removed a dose of accommodation.

official_quotes.title: FOMC post-meeting press conference (opening statement and Q&A)
official_quotes.core_quote: This morning, the FOMC decided to maintain the target rate for the federal funds rate at 3¾ to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve’s dual mandate. ... events.core_quote: On Wednesday the Federal Open Market Committee voted to raise the policy interest rate and to tighten the stance of monetary policy. I supported this decision. In tightening policy, the FOMC was responding to inflation that has remained too high for too long.

events.title: FOMC post-meeting press conference (opening statement and Q&A)

events.title: The Totality of the Data

Maintaining this modestly restrictive stance of monetary policy is entirely appropriate to achieve our maximum employment and price stability goals.

events.title: Summer of ’25: The Data

Maintaining this modestly restrictive stance of monetary policy is entirely appropriate to achieve our maximum employment and price stability goals.

events.title: Hat Tip to the Data
events.core_quote: This policy stance is appropriate given that inflation has remained above our 2 percent target while the labor market has been generally consistent with maximum employment. Looking ahead, if progress on our dual mandate goals continues as in my baseline forecast, I anticipate it will become appropriate to move interest rates toward a more neutral stance over time.

events.title: Navigating Unpredictable Terrain
events.core_quote: For these reasons, I fully supported the FOMC’s decisions to reduce the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points at each of its past two meetings. I view monetary policy as being modestly restrictive, although somewhat less so than before our recent actions. Therefore, I still see room for a further adjustment in the near term to the target range for the federal funds rate to move the stance of policy closer to the range of neutral, thereby maintaining the balance between the achievement of our two goals.

events.title: Unwavering Dedication
events.core_quote: If the economy evolves in a manner broadly consistent with my forecast, one further upward adjustment of the federal funds target range may be appropriate late this year to support a timelier return of inflation to target. But that is just my forecast, and time—and the totality of the data—will tell.

items: Weights 40/20/20/10/10, the 90-day / 30-day current stance, the ±20 camp cuts, the 10-year history half-life, the shrinkage formula, the ±25 default for an unquantified move, and interview weights (official 1.0, two-source verbatim 0.25, paraphrase 0.10, unbestätigt 0) are not validated.

The attempted mapping from a speaker's stated path to the market path at the time of the statement does not hold. The public «vs. Markt» column is therefore a direction only (more hawkish than priced, less hawkish than priced, in line with pricing, or n/a). Basis-point figures taken from market pricing, futures or odds, and proxy series names are not in this package.

The main public camp is Variant B: each member's own scored events, 90-day window, 30-day half-life, cuts at ±20. Trend is the current own-score stance minus the structural own-score lean (material at ±15). Members without a scored event in the 90-day window are labelled «nicht eingeordnet»; there is no fallback camp.

The interview layer is included at reduced weight. Reuters, Bloomberg, WSJ, FT, CNBC and similar licensed outlets are linked or given a short paraphrase at most; licensed verbatim is omitted. Unbestätigt interviews are not counted. Daly's 14.10 and 6.11 appearances remain unbestätigt (single source).

Coverage gaps remain. Daly, Powell, Kashkari, Venable and Shukla are «nicht eingeordnet». Kashkari's recent listed appearances have no official transcript. Venable's recent official messages have no current rate path. Provisional labels are kept where the in-window official record is thin.
Barkin 9.11.2026 ('The Rooms Driving the Economy') remains unresolved after two-pass A/B and a third pass (timing-urgency dispute) and is not forced into the average.
Schmid's current own-score stance is +20.2, just above the +20 Hawk cut-off. A small revision to the latest event would change the camp.

Official-transcript quotes may contain '25 basis points' or similar when that is the speaker's own wording. Those phrases are the speaker's words, not figures taken from market pricing, and are not treated as leaks (same rule as in v3.2b).

lean_history is a monthly Variant B current-stance series (90/30) reconstructed from the same scored events. A point is flagged provisional when fewer than four events sit in that 90-day window. It is not a real-time vintage of the published package.
